text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Seven Japanese Red Army members were arrested in Beirut and the Bekaa valley.
-Prime Minister Hariri will head to Rome on Sunday on two-days visit.
-A Lebanese-Syrian summit will be held in Damascus on Thursday.
-Hizbollah Chief Sheikh Nasrallah said Israel may launch a sudden attack against Lebanon.
-Hariri meets the U.S. ambassador who expects new peace developments after March.
-The state-owned Lebanese University teachers will hold a sit-in today to protest against the administration's delay in implementing some accademic decisions.
-Lebanon filed a complaint to the five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire in the country after a Lebanese woman was killed by Israeli shelling in south Lebanon on Tuesday.
-Lebanon will host the second International Telecommunications Fair for the Middle East on April 9.
-The head of the political department of PLO Kaddoumi arrives in Beirut today to discuss the regional situation with Lebanese officials.
